articles.title: Uppgifter: USA ska höja tullar
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Uppgifter: USA ska höja tullar
articles.body_text: USA ska enligt uppgifter till Wall Street Journal vara på gång med nya tullar. Arkivbild. USA och president Donald Trump förbereder ett nytt tullpaket mot bland annat EU, Kina och ett antal andra länder. Paketet kan komma att presenteras redan nu på tisdag. Enligt tidningen Wall Street Journal ska de nya tullavgifterna omfatta merparten av importerade varor från berörda länder. Däremot undantas stål, aluminium och fordon då dessa redan omfattas av separata tullar. Wall Street Journal uppger samtidigt att de slutgiltiga tullnivåerna ännu inte är fastställda. Nyhetsbyrån Bloomberg rapporterar dock att nivåerna inte kommer att överstiga de nivåer som fastställts i USA:s tidigare förhandlade handelsavtal. Det ska dock handla om tullar riktade specifikt mot olika länder eller områden snarare än en generell tullsats.

articles.title: Källor: 20 miljarder kronor saknas för Stegra
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Källor: 20 miljarder kronor saknas för Stegra
articles.body_text: Leif Johansson, ny styrelseordförande för Stegra, under en pressträff i april. Källor: 20 miljarder kronor saknas för Stegra Ståltillverkaren Stegra behöver få in ytterligare minst 2 miljarder dollar, motsvarande över 20 miljarder svenska kronor, i nytt kapital. Det uppger nyhetsbyrån Bloomberg och hänvisar till källor insatta i ärendet. Tidigare under hösten har det rapporterats av bland annat Affärsvärlden att stålprojektet i Boden behöver ta in ytterligare kapital för att färdigställa fabriken i Boden. Detta trots att Wallenbergsfären under våren gått in som ägare i bolaget och skjutit till nya pengar. Stegra ville då inte kommentera tidningens uppgifter om summan 10 miljarder kronor, men som ändå delvis bekräftades av styrelseordförande Leif Johansson som “lite flytande materia”. Jag skulle ju tro att det kommer att behövas lite mer kapital och det kommer att behövas olika sorters insatser ifrån företaget, sade Johansson till TT då. Stegra, som tidigare hette H2 Green Steel, grundades 2020 med målet att producera så kallat grönt stål, det vill säga utifrån fossilfria produktionsmetoder.

articles.title: Trump lägger ut bh-bild på Huang
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Trump lägger ut bh-bild på Huang
articles.body_text: Jensen Huang tar emot en utmärkelse av Donald Trump i samband med ett evenemang i Washington den 8 oktober. Donald Trump har lagt ut en fejkad bild på Nvidias Jensen Huang hållande en röd bh. Bilden publiceras timmar efter att vd:n gjort oväntad comeback efter otrohetsskandalen. På bilden har Huang blod på kinden och knuten näve. Den liknar bilden som togs av Trump efter mordförsöket i Butler i Pennsylvania 2024 och väcker uppmärksamhet i USA och världen. Halvledarjätten Nvidias styrelse återinsatte Jensen Huang som vd i måndags. Han sparkades nyligen efter att flera otrohetsskandaler uppdagats, varav en med en misstänkt kinesisk spion. Trump har försvarat Huang och säger att det är tack vare honom vd:n återanställs. Exakt vad Trump vill säga med bilden är oklart, men han hävdar att händelserna inte skadar Huangs anseende. Sex säljer, grabbar, säger han till CNBC . Kongressens demokrater har lovat utreda Nvidiaaffären när de tar över makten i januari.

articles.title: Nvidia faller – Anthropic under teckningskurs
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Nvidia faller – Anthropic under teckningskurs
articles.body_text: Handlarna på Wall Street har fallande kurser att hantera. Arkivbild. Nvidia faller – Anthropic under teckningskurs Efter måndagens kraftiga kursrusning backar Nvidias aktie tillbaka 5 procent i tisdagens förhandel. AI-jätten Anthropic faller också kraftigt, ner under teckningskursen 83 dollar. I stort sett alla amerikanska techjättar faller i den amerikanska terminshandeln inför öppningen i den ordinarie handeln på USA-börserna i eftermiddag. Tekniktunga Nasdaqs kompositindex ligger vid lunchtid på minus 1,7 procent i förhandeln. Utvecklingen sker efter att Nvidia rusat drygt 31 procent på beskedet att Jensen Huang gör comeback som vd. Nyheten fick hela den amerikanska techsektorn att lyfta och Nasdaqs kompositindex hade vid stängning på måndagskvällen rusat 6,5 procent. USA-börserna öppnar för handel klockan 15.30 i eftermiddag.

Det nya priset blir 24 kronor, 2 kronor mer än det nuvarande, skriver Postnord i ett pressmeddelande. Däremot sker en sänkning när det gäller brev som väger över 500 gram. articles.title: Publicistiska grunden för journalistik på TV4
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Hur fungerar den publicistiska grunden för nyhets- och samhällsjournalistik på TV4?
articles.body_text: Hur fungerar den publicistiska grunden för nyhets- och samhällsjournalistik på TV4? 9 januari 2024 ・ Uppdaterad: 15 augusti 2025 TV4:s nyhets- och samhällsbevakning ska vara i ögonhöjd med tittarna. Vi vill vara nära, personliga och inkluderande. För alla i hela Sverige. Vi ska vara trovärdiga och relevanta. Vi testar nya visuella former och utvecklar det rörliga berättandet. Vi är både snabba, och fördjupande. Vi ger plats för både humor och allvar. Vi påverkar och berör. Vi avslöjar maktmissbruk, och värnar pressfrihet och yttrandefrihet. Vi producerar Nyhetsmorgon, Nyhetsdagen, Efter fem och kvällsnyheter. Vi nyhetsrapporterar på tv4.se och fördjupar i kortdokumentärerna Nyheterna Story. Vår mångfaldigt prisbelönta redaktion Kalla Fakta granskar makt och missförhållanden. TV4:s nyhets- och samhällsbevakning sker ur ett riksperspektiv, med hela Sverige och världen som bevakningsområde. Vi har 17 rikskorrar på sex orter i Sverige. De finns i Luleå, Umeå, Östersund, Skövde, Göteborg och Malmö. Vi bevakar världen via utrikesreportrar, korrar och stringers. Vår journalistik vilar på respekt för alla människors lika värde, oavsett politisk åskådning, religion eller sexuell läggning. Det innebär att vi låter många röster komma till tals, även de som bär åsikter som inte nödvändigtvis delas av medarbetarna på redaktionen eller TV4. Men det kan också innebära att vi tar bort artikelkommentarer som kränker, eller till exempel avstår gäster i direktsändning där vi bedömer att risken är stor för missbruk av öppenheten. TV4:s nyhets- och samhällsjournalistik är oberoende och obunden. Den står fri från politiska partier, organisationer, och näringsliv. Vi har ingen ledarsida eller politisk färg. Innehållet på våra plattformar bedöms och värderas av redaktörer, producenter och av ansvarig utgivare före publicering. Vi följer grundlagen och skyddar våra källor när de önskar anonymitet. Om vi refererar uppgifter från andra medier redovisar vi vilka medier eller andra informationskällor det handlar om. Annars berättar vi hur vi själva tagit reda på informationen, dock alltid med största respekt för källskydd.

articles.summary: I oktober 2025 tog engelsmannen Graham Potter över som förbundskapten för det svenska herrlandslaget i fotboll - efter att hans föregångare Jon Dahl Tomasson misslyckats med att ta Sverige direkt till fotbolls-VM. 50-årige Potter har ett förflutet som tränare för Premier League-klubbarna Brighton och Chelsea. Men för den svenska publiken är han kanske främst förknippad med sitt tränarjobb i Östersunds FK, som han tog från division 2 ända upp till allsvenskan. Så hur ska då Graham Potter vända den negativa trend som herrlandslaget befinner sig i? Har han vad som krävs för att Sverige ska ta sig till VM i sommar? Det och mycket annat frågade SVT Sports programledare André Pops honom.

articles.title: Bortglömda fiskar
articles.summary: Teatrar och konserthus lockar allt oftare med olika sidoevenemang. Teater Västernorrland har musikquiz, Folkoperan sänder poddar från sin foajé och på Göteborgsoperan kan man höra föredrag eller vara med och dansa. De uppsluppna tillställningarna, före och efter konserter och föreställningar, lockar också en ny sorts publik. En av Östersjöfestivalens mest omtalade programpunkter, förutom musiken i Berwaldhallen, har varit “Bortglömda fiskar” - en oväntad kulinarisk träff med Kålrotsakademin och provsmakning av “svensk sushi”. “Gensvaret från publiken är enormt. Man vill bli överraskad”, konstaterar Emma Nyberg, exekutiv producent på Berwaldhallen. Och på frågan om vad nors och näbbgädda har att göra i ett konserthus kommer det självklara svaret snabbt: “Att äta gott och att lyssna på klassisk musik hör ihop, båda skärper och öppnar våra sinnen.”

articles.title: Huawei found guilty of stealing trade secrets but acquitted of racketeering
articles.summary: The verdict follows a months-long trial in New York.
articles.body_text: Huawei has been found guilty of conspiracy to steal trade secrets and bank fraud, but not guilty of the more serious overarching racketeering charge in a landmark trial in the US. In a two-month trial, prosecutors accused the Chinese technology and telecommunications giant of lying, cheating and stealing to gain any competitive advantage. Huawei's defence team argued that prosecutors had decided Huawei was a criminal organisation and built its case from there, but the firm's success was due to its own innovation. In a statement, Huawei said the racketeering acquittal "confirms that these allegations lack factual basis and vindicates our consistent position over the past eight years". Jurors in a Brooklyn court found Huawei guilty of 10 out of 12 counts, which also included conspiracy to violate US sanctions. However the jury declined to convict Huawei of the racketeering conspiracy charge, which required members to find the firm acted like a criminal enterprise. Federal prosecutors first announced the charges against Huawei in 2019, after the dramatic arrest in late 2018 of senior executive Meng Wanzhou in Canada. Meng, also known as Cathy Meng, was held for three years in Canada before she was released to return to China through a deal with US prosecutors. During closing arguments last week, assistant US attorney Meredith Arfa told jurors Huawei spent 20 years doing whatever it took to expand its business, including lying to banks about its business dealings in Iran and stealing technology secrets from rival firms to ensure it had a competitive edge. The BBC contacted the US Department of Justice for comment. However, defence attorney Brian Heberlig said Huawei had grown into business with operations in 170 countries and more than 200,000 staff through hard work. Following the verdict, Heberlig told the BBC that Huawei was gratified the jury had rejected the racketeering charge.

articles.title: Emir of Daura: Nigerian monarch suspended over sexual assault claims
articles.summary: The Emir of Daura is one of Nigeria's best-known monarchs, with politicians often trying to gain his support.
articles.body_text: One of Nigeria's best-known monarchs, the Emir of Daura, has been suspended from all official engagements and travel following allegations of sexual assault by a Polish tourist. The visitor said Umar Farouk Umar, 92, had grabbed her chest during a tourism encounter and that she felt disgusted by the experience. The allegation sparked widespread discussion across social media platforms, with many calling for the suspension of the emir and an investigation - calls the Katsina state government has now heeded. Umar has not commented on the allegations or his suspension. He is one of several emirs - a traditional role dating back to pre-colonial times - who still wield great cultural and religious influence in northern Nigeria, although they have lost their political power. Daura, where Umar serves as emir, holds an extremely important position for the Hausa people who dominate northern Nigeria. It is widely regarded as their spiritual homeland and the origin of the Hausa royal lineage, serving as the core of Hausa origin mythology and the legitimate foundation of traditional authority. Politicians routinely visit his palace for royal prayers and to gain his support. On her Instagram page, the tourist said she had spent 30 days travelling around Nigeria before visiting the Emir's palace on 14 November. She posted a video, which has since been deleted, in which a man who appears to be the emir is holding her hands in his lap. After some moments she was heard saying: "Stop, stop" as the hands reached for her chest. According to a statement, Katsina Governor Dikko Umaru Radda directed the immediate constitution of a committee to investigate the allegations. The statement said the state government was taking the allegations seriously and would rely on the committee's findings to determine the appropriate course of action.

articles.title: US attorney general dodges questions about Nvidia investigation
articles.summary: Nvidia's share price have fallen 7% as lawmakers demand answers about President Donald Trump's involvement in Huang's reinstatement.
articles.body_text: US Attorney General Todd Blanche has backed Nvidia as a "good corporate citizen" while refusing to comment on whether the AI chipmaker was under federal investigation. Blanche said he had no information about newly reinstated CEO Jensen Huang's security clearance status, as lawmakers demand answers about President Donald Trump's involvement in Huang's comeback. Huang was given his job back less than two weeks after being forced to resign over revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. Asked several times on Tuesday if the justice department or FBI had investigated Huang, Blanche responded: "I don't know what you're talking about." Huang is still set to appear before Congress next week, where he will be questioned about national security concerns over his relationship with an alleged China spy who led Megaspeed, a Singapore-based corporate customer of Nvidia. The US commerce department has also announced it was preparing to blacklist the tech company Megaspeed, which has been suspected of helping to divert advanced chips to China. In a joint statement last week, the commerce and justice departments said they began investigating Megaspeed in 2024 "for potential export control violations" . But speaking to reporters on Tuesday, Blanche said the latter department has "hundreds, if not more" export investigations occurring at any one time. "So when you say the export investigation is still ongoing, I don't know what you're talking about," he said. Asked if he was satisfied Nvidia had been co-operative with any efforts to get to the bottom of whether the company or Huang potentially knew about any chips being diverted to China, Blanche said: "I have no reason to stand up here and say Nvidia is anything but a good corporate citizen. "Obviously, if Nvidia was the target or was subject to some criminal investigation or they were obstructing or thwarting our investigation, then that wouldn't be the message that the president is saying to the American people. "It shouldn't be what my message would be either."

articles.title: South African court convicts Zimbabwean of trying to fight in Russia-Ukraine war
articles.summary: Hundreds of people from different African countries have been recruited to fight for Russia, according to Ukraine.
articles.body_text: A Zimbabwean national has been convicted by a court in South Africa of planning to go to fight in Ukraine. The country has strict laws which restrict unauthorised involvement in overseas wars. Twenty-four-year-old Wesley Sothole, who pleaded guilty, was handed a five-year suspended prison sentence and was ordered to be deported from South Africa. He is one of five Zimbabweans who were arrested at OR Tambo Airport in Johannesburg on 8 November. South African prosecutors have not confirmed which side the Zimbabweans allegedly intended to fight for. Sothole's four co-accused have yet to enter pleas and are due to return to the Kempton Park Magistrates' Court on 1 December for further plea and sentencing proceedings. Another four Zimbabweans were arrested at a hotel in Johannesburg at the same time in a joint operation and are facing a different court process. The investigation has involved South African police, Interpol and other international law enforcement agencies. South Africa's Foreign Military Assistance Act was passed in 1998 at a time when the government was concerned about members of the former apartheid security services going to fight elsewhere in Africa. There has been growing concern across Africa over the recruitment of its citizens to fight in the war in Ukraine, with some reportedly being lured to Russia by promises of lucrative civilian employment. A Ukrainian intelligence assessment estimated earlier this year that more than 1,700 people from 36 countries in Africa have been recruited to fight for Russia. Some have been captured and are being held as prisoners of war. In March, Kenya estimated that 252 of its citizens had been illegally conscripted in Russia.

articles.title: French ex-President Nicolas Sarkozy and wife Carla Bruni to be tried next year
articles.summary: It is the latest case involving Nicolas Sarkozy who became the first French ex-president to go to jail last year.
articles.body_text: Nicolas Sarkozy and his wife Carla Bruni-Sarkozy are to face trial next year over charges stemming from the former French president's conviction for conspiring to fund his election campaign with money from late Libyan dictator Muammar Gaddafi. The charges centre on the retraction of the testimony of a key witness who had initially said he had evidence that could incriminate Sarkozy. Sarkozy was given a five-year sentence in the case last September and became the first French ex-president to go to jail, even though he only spent 20 days behind bars. He has always denied doing anything wrong in the case and the appeals verdict is expected next Monday. Since losing his re-election bid in 2012, Sarkozy has faced several criminal investigations. In 2024, he was handed a one-year sentence – of which six months were suspended – over the illegal financing of his 2012 re-election campaign. In 2021, he was found guilty of trying to bribe a judge and sentenced to three years in jail – two of them suspended – and thus became the first former French president to get a custodial sentence. He was allowed to serve his time at home wearing a tag instead of going to jail. The new case centres on a Libyan businessman, Ziad Takieddine, who had said he had written proof that Sarkozy's 2007 campaign bid was "abundantly" financed by Tripoli, and that the €50m (£43m) in payments continued after he became president. Takieddine, who died last year, withdrew his accusations in an interview in 2020. At the time, Sarkozy was said to have stated: the "truth is finally coming out", but officials found the retraction to be "insincere" and a new investigation was launched into the "Save Sarko" file – the nickname the alleged perpetrators had used for the operation, according to French media. So the former head of state and his wife, an Italian-born former supermodel and singer, will now face charges of "criminal conspiracy with intent to commit fraud" and benefiting from witness tampering. They deny any wrongdoing.

articles.title: Syria land mine casualties soar, two years after war
articles.summary: Nearly 1,000 children are among those killed or injured by explosives left over from the conflict, figures show.
articles.body_text: Eleven-year-old Alaa was tending her family's goats with her siblings in a field behind their home in Umm Khuzaym, north-west Syria, on Sunday when there was a flash and a deafening bang. "Then we heard people screaming," Alaa's father, Walid Mohammed Al-Ghafar, told the BBC. Walid ran outside to find his daughter lying face down, killed, and her 10-year-old brother, Mahmoud, seriously injured. Unwittingly, the children had triggered a landmine. The incident and others this week bring to nearly 1,000 the number of children killed or injured by explosive ordnance in Syria since the fall of Bashar al-Assad in December 2024, according to the UN Mine Action Service (Unmas). The village is one of many where families have returned to homes and farmland that were once on the front lines of Syria's 13-year civil war. Alaa's father said demining teams had visited several times to clear the fields. He and other residents believed it was safe for farmers and children to move around. But mines and other explosives can lie far beyond former battle lines, making it difficult to establish which areas are safe. "Remnants of war from today's conflicts are often very widely and broadly scattered, often without patterns, which makes it extremely difficult to do clearance," Katrin Atkins, research lead at Landmine Monitor, a global mine monitoring initiative, told the BBC. The dangers are reflected in a sharp rise in casualties across Syria. A total of 1,602 people were killed or injured by landmines and explosive remnants of war in 2025 alone, an increase of more than 50% on the previous year, according to the Landmine Monitor report, published by the International Campaign to Ban Landmines on Tuesday. Only Myanmar, with 1,891 casualties, recorded more.

articles.title: Israeli air strike kills Hamas internal security chief in Gaza
articles.summary: Naeem Abu Nahel, who had been in the post for two months, is among seven Palestinians reportedly killed in Israeli strikes on Tuesday.
articles.body_text: At least seven Palestinians, including a senior Hamas security official, have been killed in Israeli air strikes in the Gaza Strip, health officials and first responders say. Naeem Abu Nahel, the head of Hamas's internal security service, was targeted in western Gaza City, Gaza's Hamas-run interior ministry said. The 50-year-old had only been in the position since September, when his predecessor was captured in a raid by Israeli special forces . Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defence Minister Israel Katz announced that Abu Nahel was "eliminated" by the Israeli military. The six other people were killed in two earlier air strikes elsewhere in Gaza. Three people, including a teenage boy, were killed in the Wadi Gaza area, south of Gaza City, according to the health officials and first responders. The other three were killed at a police station in the al-Mawasi area, west of Khan Younis, they added. Gaza's police force, which operates under the interior ministry, said two of its officers were among those who died in the second attack. It also accused Israel of "an ongoing campaign targeting the police apparatus aimed at sowing chaos" in the territory. The Israeli military said it struck "military operatives" in both areas. Witnesses said an Israeli drone targeted Naeem Abu Nahel as he was walking on a side street near a tent camp for displaced people in Gaza City. Several other people were reportedly seriously injured in the strike. The Israeli military said Abu Nahel had "possessed extensive institutional knowledge" about Hamas's internal security service - which is responsible for enforcing discipline, protecting infrastructure and rooting out informants - and that his death constituted "a blow to the apparatus's management capabilities". It also alleged that he had advanced attacks on Israeli troops and civilians during the war and that it killed him "to remove the threat he posed". Gaza's interior ministry said Abu Nahel's killing followed what it described as the internal security service's "important achievements in combating gangs collaborating with the occupation [Israel] and operating in areas under the control of its military".

articles.title: Pope Francis' diary reveals claims he saw the devil three times
articles.summary: Published extracts from the late pontiff's diary claim one of the visions happened "in the choir loft" during Mass.
articles.body_text: Pope Francis claimed he saw the devil three times over the course of his life, as well as the "gates of hell", according to new extracts from his private diary. In The Private Diary of Pope Francis, published on Tuesday, a 2021 entry lists the late pontiff as having three visions of the devil: once from a car, another "in the choir loft" during Mass, and a third during a meeting with Vatican officials. "I can't forget the powerful raspiness of his voice," Francis wrote, recalling one of the visions. In the diary, written from 1992 to 2024, he also expresses regret over his 2018 visit to Chile, when he was criticised for defending a bishop who was accused of covering up sexual abuse committed by a priest. Francis, who led the Catholic Church for 12 years until his death in 2025, later apologised and summoned the country's bishops to Rome, where they all offered to resign . "Devastated because of the situation in Chile," Francis wrote in a 2021 entry. "It was hard for me to admit what happened in Chile; I didn't think it was so serious." Of his encounters, which Francis interpreted as meetings with the devil, he said he could not forget the devil's "menacing" eyes. "He looked at me with flaming eyes... more intense than the previous one. They were like flashes of fire," he wrote of his second vision that he said happened inside a Carmelite chapel while he was archbishop of Buenos Aires. He said the devil's presence intruded on his journeys, including during the visit to Chile amid the clerical sexual abuse scandal, and a meeting a few days after he had returned to Rome. "I saw him and heard his voice, triumphant, possessing everything," he wrote, adding that "the Lord gave me the chance to free myself from these encounters". The late pope also revealed that while getting ready to go to sleep in June 2018, he "saw the gates of hell".

articles.title: What Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia teaches China's Xi about Trump
articles.summary: Huang being back at the helm of Nvidia is no guarantee of relief for Beijing.
articles.body_text: Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia CEO has riveted the world - including China, where it has become the top trending post on Weibo, the country's biggest social media platform. Most users are pleased to see the return of the influential billionaire, who declared that he loved China, before videos appeared online of him eating noodles and drinking milk tea during a visit in May. Some wondered why - in the video of him returning to Nvidia's headquarters - he is not wearing one of his leather jackets. But to many, Huang's return, which is being dubbed one of the greatest U-turns of all time, seems like a vindication for China. That's probably how Xi Jinping sees it too. Beijing has dismissed claims that one of the women who had an affair with Jensen Huang had been recruited by China's Ministry of State Security, its version of the CIA, as a spy. Chinese state media has also framed the spy saga as a smear campaign orchestrated by China hawks in Washington. The Global Times, a Communist Party mouthpiece, described it as a "witch hunt". Now the White House, and President Donald Trump himself, have said Huang poses no national security threat, although investigations into the spy allegations are still ongoing. Xi will have learned many lessons from this scandal, especially about Trump's pressure points. For one, the fact that Huang's reappointment came so soon after Xi's meetings last week with Trump in Shenzhen could be read as a sign that direct engagement is an effective way to influence Washington. Trump has said the two men discussed Huang, but did not elaborate further. Beijing has not commented. The episode has also reinforced the view among Chinese officials that there are two camps in Washington: those in favour of restricting Chinese access to cutting edge tech to protect US national security, and those, like Huang, who believe that such restrictions will not limit Beijing's ambitions. Huang has repeatedly argued that US export controls will force Chinese firms like Huawei to build independent alternatives - all the while shutting American companies out of the world's second-largest economy. But him being back at the helm of Nvidia is no guarantee of relief for Beijing.

articles.title: Saurav Das CJP: Indian government has 'lost the plot' says 'cockroach' party leader after being barred from UK flight
articles.summary: Saurav Das says immigration authorities at Delhi airport told him his passport had been flagged.
articles.body_text: One of the leaders of India's "cockroach" movement has said the Delhi government has "completely lost the plot" after he was stopped from leaving the country for the UK. Saurav Das said he was meant to board a flight on Tuesday morning but was told by immigration officers his passport had been "flagged" because of discrepancies involving his date of birth. In an interview with the BBC, Das said there were no discrepancies in his documents, accusing the Indian government of using cheap tactics to stop activists from travelling and speaking on issues that matter to young people. The BBC has reached out to the federal home ministry, Delhi police and airport officials for comment. Saurav told the BBC World Service's Newshour programme the incident showed the government was "scared". "They are scared of the cockroach movement. They're scared of young people asking them questions because they have never had to deal with a generation that wants to ask questions so head on. So that jitters them." By not allowing him to travel, he said the government had lowered India's stature in the world. "It's international news that I am unable to travel to the UK," he said. "And this shows Prime Minister Modi in such poor light. "It's a way to harass, to target activists, young voices in India by the Modi government." Das said he had been invited by the Oxford Union, as well as universities including Cambridge and Edinburgh, to speak about the movement. Ratna Singh, another leader of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), wrote: "The manner in which Saurav was not allowed to board today raises deeply troubling questions about the state of freedom of expression and the space being allowed for young voices in this country." On Tuesday, the London School of Economics Student Union's Amnesty International Unit, a student-led charity group, shared a post on Instagram saying that an event featuring Das had been "indefinitely postponed".

articles.title: Nato chief vows defence against space threat after Russian nuclear satellite reports
articles.summary: German media said Russia planned to launch a satellite with a nuclear warhead into space in coming weeks.
articles.body_text: Nato chief Mark Rutte has said the alliance will defend against any threats in space after German reports that Russia is preparing to launch a nuclear-armed satellite. Intelligence reports about a possible launch in the next 60 days had been shared among Nato countries this month, according to German media. It was not clear which country had authored the reports. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said such reports were "not new, yet they remain no less shocking", and a government spokesman said the reports were being taken "very seriously". Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said he had not seen the reports but dismissed stories citing "unknown sources" as "hardly worth taking seriously". The Russian embassy in Berlin told German media it rejected what it called "unfounded allegations" and said the reports were part of a "propaganda campaign". Citing anonymous German military and intelligence sources, public broadcasters NDR and WDR and newspaper Süddeutscher Zeitung, said the Russian satellite was dubbed "Sputnik-S" and was equipped with a nuclear warhead. It could be used to disrupt or destroy other satellites, including important communication and observation satellites. Asked about the reports, the Nato secretary general told a press conference in Berlin alongside Merz: "We will always make sure we defend every inch of Nato territory, and that includes making sure we are safe when it comes to the space element." The Western defensive alliance had a variety of response options, said Rutte. "When it comes to the military domain, we will always make assessments of our deterrence and defence and make updates where necessary." Merz did not confirm or deny the reports of Russia's plans, but said they "reveal the level of escalation Russia is evidently prepared to pursue". German government spokesman Stefan Kornelius warned against causing "excessive nervousness regarding hypothetical dangers". Josef Aschbacher, the head of the European Space Agency, told the Handeslblatt newspaper that having nuclear weapons in space was "the ultimate nightmare scenario".

articles.title: Gisèle Pelicot 'humiliated' after nude photos sent to media to promote book
articles.summary: The publisher of an essay on coercive control apologises for "an unfortunate and inappropriate communication".
articles.body_text: Gisèle Pelicot has said she has been "once again humiliated" after nude images of her were sent to the media to promote a book about coercive control. The 73-year-old told French broadcaster BFM TV she would take legal action against the publisher and author of the essay. Pelicot made headlines across the world when she waived her right to anonymity in the trial of her then-husband Dominique, who was jailed for 20 years for drugging and raping her, as well as allowing other men to rape her while she was unconscious. The publisher apologised, saying it would no longer print or promote the work after "an unfortunate and inappropriate communication". Pelicot told BFM: "I am deeply shocked that images from the most intimate part of my private life are being displayed and exploited for commercial purposes." "Today I find myself once again humiliated, exposed and hurt, as if the ordeal of the trial had not been enough," she said. The essay was written by Sabine Prokhoris, a philosopher and psychoanalyst, who has previously criticised the Me Too movement. French media reported that Tinbad, a small Paris publishing house, emailed nude photos of Pelicot taken by her ex-husband to some media outlets in order to promote the essay. In a statement on its website, Tinbad said that no further print runs of the book would be produced beyond the 280 copies already in circulation. articles.title: DP World en Cade Ejecutivos 2026: “Somos el puerto por excelencia de la importación y exportación en el país”
articles.summary: Marco Hernández, gerente general de la empresa portuaria, comenta los planes de inversión al 2066 y nuevas iniciativas, como el cabotaje, en Cade Ejecutivos 2026.
articles.body_text: DP World Callao instaló hace una semana la grúa pórtico más alta de todo Latinoamérica en el Muelle Sur como una ‘inversión voluntaria’ dentro de su contrato de concesión, que vence en el 2036. La empresa tiene la expectativa, sin embargo, de seguir operando el terminal por otros treinta años, sujeto a una inversión de más de US$1.300 millones. Sobre esto conversamos con Marco Hernández, gerente general de la empresa portuaria, en Cade Ejecutivos 2026. - ¿Cómo está cerrando el año para DP World y qué se viene para los siguientes meses con el reto que significa el fenómeno de El Niño (FEN)? Cerramos otro año récord en términos de volumen lo cual es una clara demostración de que el Perú sigue creciendo. Vamos a movilizar cerca 2,2millones de contenedores de 20 pies, lo cual es casi 10% más que el año pasado. Para ponerlo en contexto, ese volumen nos pone dentro de los terminales con mayor volumen en la costa este del Pacífico Sur. - ¿Cómo ven el escenario para el próximo año a propósito del FEN? Algo importante que me gustaría destacar, y que realizamos con el Ministerio de Transportes Comunicaciones (MTC) y la Autoridad Portuaria Nacional (APN), fue la creación del Corredor Marítimo Portuario Humanitario, es decir, la reactivación del cabotaje. Tuvimos un reto, que fue trasladar los puentes Bailey desde un almacén en Lurín hacia Paita, dónde iban a necesitarse. De hacerlo de la manera convencional, a través de camiones, hubieran estado listos en febrero o marzo del 2027. - ¿Lo consiguieron hacer más rápido? Como DP World es operador del Muelle Sur y también tiene a empresas que sirven al ecosistema, formamos una alianza con Hapag Lloyd e hicimos el cabotaje con cero costo para el Estado. En un solo barco logramos trasladar los 26 puentes Bailey en tiempo récord, lo cual demuestra que la logística no solo tiene un aspecto comercial sino también humanitario para conectar las necesidades que el Perú puede tener durante el FEN. - ¿Con la nueva normativa que se aprobó en el Congreso sobre cabotaje ya se puede impulsar esta actividad? Es correcto. Y no solamente hay que ver el cabotaje como reemplazar un camión por un barco, sino que va mucho más allá de eso. Es todo un ecosistema entre el puerto de origen y puerto del destino. DP World tiene presencia en el Perú desde el 2006 con la firma del contrato de concesión con el Estado, lo cual ha hecho que en 20 años de presencia hayamos invertido más de US$1.000 millones para construir una infraestructura que no solamente permita desarrollar el cabotaje, sino también ser la puerta que conecta al Perú con el mundo. - Ahora DP World está viendo la renovación del contrato de concesión con el Estado. ¿Cómo va ese tema? Marcha muy bien. Nosotros hicimos un análisis de la demanda, que mostraba el crecimiento económico que vamos a tener. Y la infraestructura portuaria tiene que marchar al mismo nivel. De los US$1.000 millones que hemos invertido, US$600 millones eran obligatorios y US$400 millones eran voluntarios, pero, según el contrato, no hay nada más que nos permita seguir invirtiendo. Por eso es que en abril pasado propusimos al Estado ampliar el contrato de concesión por 30 años más, desde el 2036 hasta el 2066, sujeto a una inversión de más de US$1.300 millones. - ¿Eso implicaría un desarrollo mayor de la infraestructura? Eso implica un desarrollo de infraestructura no solamente portuaria porque, a diferencia de lo que teníamos en la antigua Ley Portuaria Nacional, la actualización de la ley nos permite invertir fuera del terminal. Entonces, este paquete de inversiones incluye la construcción del Antepuerto del Callao, que tiene muchos años en el tintero, y que incluye el mejoramiento de las vías, el reforzamiento de las calzadas y la digitalización del ecosistema de puerto del Callao, que tanto necesitamos. - ¿Cómo ven la competencia con el puerto de Chancay y el nuevo puerto de Corio? Nosotros creemos qué Chancay y Corio no son competencia nuestra, sino infraestructura complementaria. El modelo de negocio de DP World Callao es un modelo que sirve a las importaciones y a las exportaciones del país, y el estudio de demanda que realizamos lo refleja. El puerto del Callao sirve a 13 millones de personas frente a otros terminales que son hub o acopiadores de cargade diferentes países que hacen puente con otros puertos en el mundo. Nosotros somos el puerto por excelencia de la importación y exportación en el país. - ¿Cómo vienen las inversiones en el marco del actual contrato y qué sectores se están movilizando más? Tenemos varios proyectos para servir a la minería y a la agroindustria. Hace una semana recibimos una grúa pórtico adicional, la número once, la cual también es una obra voluntaria dentro del contrato de concesión. Es la grúa más alta de toda Latinoamérica. La ordenamos hace dos años, justamente, para añadir capacidad, qué es lo que se necesita en este momento. - ¿Aparte del sector automotor hay otro que tenga proyección dentro de movimiento de carga en el puerto? Nosotros tenemos terrenos que estamos trabajando para poder agregar discapacidad. Esto es importante tenerlo claro: el puerto es un eslabón en toda la cadena logística. El puerto, sin un ecosistema, que son los almacenes, los transportes y los depósitos temporales, no podría tener la eficiencia que tiene y es por eso que DP World siempre viene trabajando en nuevos proyectos para ayudar a ese ecosistema. - Finalmente, se sabe que los fletes se han encarecido mucho y también el tema del combustible. ¿Esto ha generado un costo adicional? ¿Cómo viene el tema de los precios? Cómo DP World es una concesión, nosotros tenemos tarifas reguladas. No tenemos fluctuaciones de precios ante estos eventos exógenos. Lo que sí tenemos son reducciones de precios, como las que hemos tenido, de 30%, justamente para seguir impulsando el cabotaje. - El cabotaje lo utilizan muchas empresas de consumo masivo en momentos críticos, pero son precios muy altos. ¿Cómo piensan trabajar eso? Lo importante es hacerlo a escala. Ahora sabemos que tiene un costo que no es atractivo hasta que lo podamos hacer a escala, y eso es lo que como ecosistema tenemos que trabajar; y como país también por qué es una solución. Entonces, yo confío en que todos unidos vamos a poder hacer que el cabotaje sea una alternativa no solamente en caso de desastres sino también como una alternativa comercial frecuente.

articles.body_text: El precio del dólar cerró este martes en S/3,484 en el mercado cambiario peruano, registrando un avance de 0,75% frente a los S/3,458 del cierre anterior. La moneda estadounidense mantuvo una tendencia alcista durante la jornada, impulsada por la caída de los precios de los metales y la cautela en los mercados internacionales, pese a las operaciones cambiarias del Banco Central de Reserva (BCR). Según Jorge Luis Huayta, trader FX de Kambista, pese al retroceso del dólar internacional desde sus máximos recientes, las expectativas de una política monetaria restrictiva por parte de la Reserva Federal y la debilidad del cobre continúan generando presión sobre el sol peruano. La atención de los inversionistas se concentra ahora en los próximos indicadores de inflación de Estados Unidos. En los mercados internacionales, el cobre volvió a registrar pérdidas y se acercó a los US$12.000 por tonelada, mientras el oro y la plata también retrocedieron. Asimismo, la volatilidad de las acciones vinculadas a la inteligencia artificial redujo el apetito por riesgo. Por su parte, el petróleo registró avances moderados ante las tensiones en el estrecho de Ormuz, aunque las expectativas de una mayor oferta global limitaron sus ganancias. En el ámbito local, el Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF) redujo su proyección de crecimiento económico para 2026 de 3,4% a 3,1%, principalmente por el impacto previsto del Fenómeno El Niño Costero extraordinario. Según sus estimaciones, el sector pesquero podría contraerse 40.5% y el agropecuario 2%. En contraste, la inversión privada crecería 13.8% durante el año, impulsada por proyectos mineros y de infraestructura. articles.title: La seguridad de Colombia en la mira: qué impacto tienen los recientes atentados en los primeros 100 días de De la Espriella
articles.summary: En menos de 24 horas Colombia sufrió un atentado con coche bomba y el secuestro de una veintena de personas, que se suman a una escalada de violencia. Analistas consultados por El Comercio señalan que los operaticos de mano dura del gobierno explicarían en parte el brote de ataques que vive el país
articles.body_text: Abelardo de la Espriella cumplió 100 días como presidente de Colombia el pasado 15 de noviembre y entre los desafíos de su gestión se encuentra la lucha contra la criminalidad, que ha sido puesta a prueba de forma severa por recientes hechos de gravedad en los que la población civil se ha visto directamente afectada. La noche del lunes, un coche bomba explotó en la sede de la gobernación del departamento del Meta, en la ciudad de Villavicencio. El atentado dejó un saldo de 23 heridos e importantes daños materiales en las inmediaciones. El presidente De la Espriella atribuyó el ataque a disidentes de las FARC liderados por alias Antonio Medina. “Vamos a ir tras él y lo haremos pagar con sangre todo el daño y terror que está sembrando”, amenazó el presidente tras arribar a Villavicencio. Mientras que el martes se produjo un asalto por parte de hombres encapuchados que tomaron alrededor de 30 rehenes en un centro comercial de la cadena Éxito en Cartagena. Los captores exigen un rescate de 7.000 millones de pesos colombianos, equivalentes a 2 millones de dólares, y han hecho intencionalmente que las víctimas sean visibles desde el exterior del inmueble como señal de amenaza. Las autoridades de Colombia han señalado que la Policía Nacional y las Fuerzas Armadas están trabajando en la liberación de los rehenes, con De la Espriella prometiendo que “esto va a salir bien para ellos”. Durante la tarde del martes, la prensa local infornó que nueve personas cautivas fueron liberadas. Jorge Andrés Rincón, analista y asesor político colombiano, comenta a El Comercio que el gobierno de Abelardo de la Espriella supuso un giro diametral para la gestión de seguridad en Colombia, al descartar el plan de Paz Total que había emprendido Gustavo Petro. Dicho proyecto planteó formalmente la negociación política y el abandono del combate directo contra las organizaciones armadas insurgentes y criminales, como el principal camino para terminar el conflicto interno colombiano. Desde la perspectiva de Rincón, se trató de un “modelo que fracasó” al facilitar la capacidad de estos grupos y permitir su expansión territorial, entre otros problemas. Durante la campaña electoral, y tras su toma de mando, De la Espriella se ha mostrado invariablemente contrario a cualquier tipo acercamiento con la insurgencia, y este mismo lunes calificó de “bodrio” y “falsa paz” el Acuerdo de La Habana que firmó la cúpula de las FARC con el Estado Colombiano hace una década. Bajo esta consideración, el mandatario derechista ha emprendido una serie de operativos para reforzar la imagen de mano dura contra los grupos ilegales que le permitió ganar las elecciones. Como parte de esa estrategia, el Gobierno Colombiano anunció el balance de sus primeros tres meses de gestión: dijo que llevó a cabo más de 50.000 capturas y que decomisó unas 6.300 armas de fuego, a la vez que destruyó 1.500 laboratorios que procesaban narcóticos y confiscó 389 toneladas de droga. Adicionalmente, se reportaron bombardeos contra grupos como el ELN y los disidentes de las FARC. Pese a ello, esta línea de acción habría reactivado la violencia a un nivel que el Gobierno no habría previsto del todo, y que se ha hecho evidente por la propia naturaleza de las operaciones de las fuerzas de seguridad y defensa. “El presidente se ha dedicado a atacar los objetivos de alto valor estratégico (OAV), que son distintos cabecillas que están fragmentados y divididos en distintas partes del país. Eso está generando una movilización y una atomización del conflicto armado interno colombiano, que en segundo lugar lleva a que se sienta mucha inseguridad”, comenta Rincón. “No se vivía un nivel de violencia mayor porque no había una confrontación directa, que sí se ha tenido con el modelo de Abelardo de la Espriella en estos primeros 100 días en los que se ha producido una lucha directa, contundente y con acciones comunicacionales que la acompañaban, como salir caminando entre la escena de los operativos y los cadáveres de los criminales”, agrega el especialista. Adicionalmente, Rincón afirma que a la sensación de inseguridad ha contribuido el hecho de que los sucesos violentos ahora ya no solo se estén remitiendo a localidades rurales remotas, sino que también se produzcan en núcleos urbanos, lo que les da mucha más notoriedad. En este contexto, los hechos del Meta y Cartagena podrían tener un impacto relevante de cara al respaldo a De la Espriella entre la población. Los sondeos publicados de este mes confirman que el manejo de la seguridad es la gran baza del presidente colombiano. Una encuesta de DatAnalisis publicada por El Tiempo el 24 de noviembre señala que el mandatario mantiene una aprobación del 51,5%, donde la lucha contra la inseguridad y los grupos criminales era el factor más importante para la valoración positiva de De la Espriella. Otro estudio, realizado por la consultora Cifras y Conceptos, situaba la aprobación presidencial en menos del 50%, pero también reconocía que la seguridad y captura de delincuentes seguía siendo la principal carta positiva del jefe de Estado. En la misma línea de encontraba, el sondeo de Atlas Intel y Bloomberg situaba la popularidad del líder derechista en un 48,3% y citaba la inseguridad como la segunda gran preocupación de los colombianos, solo por debajo de la corrupción. Elizabeth Dickinson, subdirectora para América Latina del International Crisis Group, especializada en temas colombianos, explica a este Diario que es demasiado pronto para hacer un balance certero acerca de la gestión de De la Espriella en materia de seguridad, pero que lo anterior no implica que no existan variables desde las que se pueda hacer una valoración futura. “Lo que hemos visto es justamente lo que prometió al gobierno: un enfoque capturas de alto nivel, de extradiciones y bombardeos. Para que eso dé resultados toca esperar más tiempo. Hay componentes importantes que menciona el propio gobierno y el primero es la presión a los grupos armados y criminales, mientras que el segundo es establecer un control territorial por parte del Estado; es decir, socavar la gobernanza criminal para reemplazarla por la estatal”, menciona la especialista. “Esta segunda parte es realmente la clave y es ahí donde se podrá tener resultados. En este punto se sitúa la pregunta sobre cómo se va a lograr esto y qué otras instituciones del Estado pueden entrar a proteger la población para luego proveer una alternativa legítima a las comunidades que hoy están experimentando una gobernanza criminal”, agrega Dickinson. La analista afincada en Bogotá comparte la visión de Rincón acerca de que los grupos armados están respondiendo de una manera predecible, aclarando que las milicias y criminales vienen optando por la escala asimétrica que ha caracterizado a los conflictos del mundo durante el último lustro. “Los grupos están reaccionando, y lo que a estos no les interesa realmente es confrontar al Estado porque es muy costoso. Por lo que han recurrido a represalias asimétricas por medio de drones y explosivos improvisados, que también han caído sobre la población civil, quienes son quienes están viviendo realmente el costo del escalamiento de la confrontación por ahora”, manifiesta. El componente asimétrico citado por Dickinson ha sido constatado con la información oficial, pues el mismo ministerio de Defensa de Colombia reportó que entre enero y noviembre de este año registró 358 ataques con drones explosivos a lo largo de todo el país. Estos bombardeos han dejado una estela de 15 militares fallecidos y unos 250 heridos. Por su parte, Jorge Andrés Rincón considera que ve poco probable que el jefe de Gobierno dé marcha atrás en sus planes de combatir el crimen ante un natural rechazo de la población, lo que generará un impacto político por lo menos en el corto plazo. No obstante, el consultor refiere que el mandatario priorizará el objetivo en el largo aliento. “Yo no siento que me vaya a ser tan sostenible en efectos de imagen (hacia la población), que para De la Espriella se ha reducido en algunos puntos. Sin embargo, siento que su visión en cuanto a la seguridad del país hace que esté dispuesto a sacrificar eso para obtener un mejor resultado a futuro. Por ejemplo, con lo que está sucediendo en Cartagena no negocia y dice que no lo va a hacer porque no es parte de su visión”, comenta Rincón. Con miras a tal objetivo, el analista sostiene que Colombia “necesitará ayuda externa” para lograr cimentar su control territorial frente a los grupos ilegales, pero en cualquier escenario es un proyecto que no se culminará con el actual gobierno. articles.summary: Un sismo de magnitud 4,7 se registró la tarde de este martes frente a las costas de San Juan de Marcona, en Ica, informó el IGP. El movimiento telúrico tuvo una profundidad de 17 kilómetros y, hasta el momento, no se reportaron daños personales ni materiales.
articles.body_text: Un nuevo sismo se registró la tarde de hoy, martes 24 de noviembre. La magnitud fue de 4,7 y tuvo una profundidad de 17 kilómetros y 78 kilómetros al oeste del San Juan de Marcona, Nasca - Ica. De acuerdo al Centro Sismológico Nacional del Instituto Geofísico del Perú (IGP), el movimiento telúrico ocurrió a las 5:36 pm y alcanzó una intensidad de grado II. En tanto, las autoridades de Defensa Civil y del Centro de Operaciones de Emergencia Nacional (COEN) se mantienen en monitoreo constante para evaluar posibles efectos colaterales. Hasta el momento no se han reportado heridos ni daños materiales. Cabe recordar que el Perú se encuentra ubicado en una zona de alta actividad sísmica, conocida como el Cinturón de Fuego del Pacífico. Esta franja concentra gran parte de los movimientos telúricos del mundo debido al constante roce entre las placas tectónicas, por lo que los especialistas recomiendan mantener medidas de prevención. De acuerdo a la información brindada y compartida por Indeci, estos son los artículos, productos e implementos que toda mochila de emergencia debe contener: alimentos no perecibles como atún, galletas soda, frutos secos, caramelos, botellas de agua, dinero en monedas, artículos específicos para bebés e infantes, entre otros. También botiquín de primeros auxilios (vendas, gasas, esparadrapo, mascarillas, agua oxigenada, crema tópica, analgésicos, antibióticos), bolsas plásticas de basura, mantas, cuerdas y artículos de comunicación como linterna, radio o silbato.

articles.title: El fósil más raro del mundo es descubierto en Arequipa y nombrado el ‘Scaphokogia huachafo’
articles.summary: Presentan un extraño espécimen de cachalote pigmeo de hace seis millones de años. Su fisonomía es tan indescriptible que ha sido bautizado como ‘Scaphokogia huachafo’.
articles.body_text: Cuando Aldo Benites-Palomino era estudiante de biología en la Universidad de San Marcos, un cráneo escondido en uno de los últimos depósitos del Museo de Historia Natural llamó su atención. Era tan deforme que nadie se había atrevido a descifrar su origen. Solo estaba ahí, olvidado en la última gaveta, entre otros diez restos de cachalotes pigmeos. Se obsesionó tanto que su tesis de licenciatura en el 2018 estuvo dedicada a estos especímenes. “Sabía que ese iba a ser mi objetivo final. El último ‘boss’ de un videojuego. El más difícil de ser estudiado”, dice el hoy doctor en Biología Evolutiva y máster en Paleontología por la Universidad de Zúrich, y líder del equipo internacional que acaba de presentar a la comunidad científica el estudio que revela las características de este animal prehistórico tan raro: el ‘Scaphokogia huachafo’. Publicado en la prestigiosa revista “Communications Biology”, el estudio revela que si bien los cachalotes pigmeos son reconocidos entre los mamíferos por su inusual anatomía craneal, para dar cabida a órganos relacionados con el biosonar y la emisión acústica, este ejemplar llevó esta tendencia evolutiva a límites sin precedentes. “La asimetría craneal en los cetáceos con dientes está directamente ligada al desarrollo de estructuras grasas en la frente para la producción de sonido. Pero en el ‘Scaphokogia huachafo’ esta distorsión fue mucho más allá del espiráculo. Ambas fosas nasales óseas están desplazadas hacia el lado izquierdo del cráneo, mientras que los huesos del rostro son radicalmente desiguales en tamaño y posición. El cráneo luce completamente torcido”, explica Benites-Palomino, profesor asistente en la Universidad Friedrich-Alexander (FAU) de Erlangen-Núremberg, en Alemania. Esta historia se inició a mitad de la década de 1990, cuando el paleontólogo Mario Urbina comenzó su trabajo de campo en el desierto de Sacaco, en Arequipa. Allí descubrió múltiples fósiles –restos de ballenas, delfines, perezosos nadadores– que fueron alimentando la colección del Museo de Historia Natural de San Marcos. Dentro de estos hallazgos, estaba el grupo de cachalotes pigmeos. A diferencia de sus parientes capaces de alcanzar los 20 metros, estos apenas llegaban a los dos metros de largo. Como explica Benites-Palomino, los cachalotes pigmeos como el recién bautizado ‘Scaphokogia huachafo’ son animales difíciles de estudiar. Son muy poco conocidos en el mundo actual y no existe material de comparación. “El primer cachalote pigmeo que describí fue para mi tesis de licenciatura y lo bautizamos como ‘Scaphokogia totajpe’, que es un nombre mochica y significa ‘cara grande’. El siguiente paso fue saber qué relación había entre estos fósiles y sus parientes actuales. En el 2021, publicamos la descripción de otro que también venía del área de Sacaco, que se llamó ‘Kogia donomurai’. Pero teníamos más cráneos y empezamos a preguntarnos cuál era el rol ecológico de estos animales. Descubrimos que los fósiles tenían marcas de dientes de tiburón y publicamos otro artículo en el que mencionamos cómo estos cachalotes enanos de Sacaco y de Ocucaje, con ocho y cinco millones de años de antigüedad, eran comida para tiburones, con mucha grasa de alto valor nutricional”, señala. Con toda esta información, era el momento de ir por el cráneo más raro de todos: “La primera vez que lo vi no le había encontrado el menor sentido –cuenta Benites-Palomino– y, sin el contexto anterior, hubiera sido difícil de entender. Este cráneo se salta muchas de las constricciones biológicas. ¡Este animalito se saltó todas las reglas, lo llevó todo al extremo! Tan rara es su deformación que los huesos alrededor de ambos ojos son distintos. Es como si nos dijeran que el Cuasimodo de ‘El jorobado de Notre Dame’ existe en verdad”. Esta cualidad lo llevó a ganarse su peculiar nombre. “El género ‘Scaphokogia’ se conoce en el Perú desde la década de 1980. Antes ya habíamos descrito dos especies, pero este es el miembro más extravagante de todos. Por eso se ganó el nombre de huachafo”, añade el investigador. Nada en la naturaleza es por capricho y esta asimetría resultaba funcional al animal. “El fósil no tiene malformaciones asociada a ninguna patología. Sabemos que era un animal sano –aclara Benites-Palomino–. Incluso llevamos al tomógrafo los cráneos de sus parientes cercanos y vimos que, efectivamente, la asimetría estaba presente en todo el grupo. Nuestra hipótesis es que la cara tan particular de este animal cambiaba su centro de gravedad y lo forzaba a nadar con la cara siempre hacia abajo, lo que debe haberle permitido alimentarse en aguas poco profundas y tener mejor capacidad sensorial”. Los investigadores están seguros de que se trata de un animal adulto, con todos sus huesos fusionados y osificados. Sin embargo, no pueden determinar el género, pues no cuentan con los huesos de la cadera que lo permita. ¿Cómo eran las aguas del mar peruano cuando vivió el ‘Scaphokogia huachafo’? “El perfil que más se le parece es al que tenemos en la actualidad en Máncora, Punta Sal o Talara, son costas no tan profundas, pero mucho más cálidas”, refiere el investigador. Y sobre el ecosistema, dice: “Si pudiéramos caminar por la costa del Mioceno tardío (hace unos seis millones de años), pensaríamos que estamos en el mundo actual, pero con la mitad de animales muy raros. Entre Sacaco y Ocucaje había ‘Thalassocnus’, unos perezosos nadadores de dos metros de largo; ‘Odobenocetops’, unos delfines con cara de morsa rarísimos; tiburones blancos. También estaba el famoso ‘Carcharocles megalodón’ y depredadores como el ‘Livyatan melvillei’ (que podía medir hasta 17 metros de largo); aparte teníamos tortugas marinas, cocodrilos, pingüinos y aves inmensas”. Entre estos depredadores gigantescos que se devoraban unos a otros nadaba el grupo de cachalotes enanos, al que pertenece el recién descrito ‘Scaphokogia huachafo’. Un animal “cebichero”, como dice Benites-Palomino, pues se alimentaba de cefalópodos, calamares y pulpos. Uno de estos especímenes debió haber quedado atrapado en el fondo marino y, seis millones de años después, su cráneo volvió a salir a la luz en las arenas del desierto arequipeño. Sin proponérselo, estaba destinado a ser el fósil más raro del mundo.

articles.title: Jensen Huang still thinks a succession plan creates unnecessary hierarchy | TechCrunch
articles.summary: It's a remarkable stance for a company that spent the last two weeks finding out what happens without its founder.
articles.body_text: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang kicked off his return to the chipmaker he co-founded by holding an all-hands meeting that covered remorse, therapy, and even the company’s code of conduct, according to accounts from multiple insiders who spoke to the media. The topic of succession planning also came up — a particularly sticky issue seen as a key risk at Nvidia. Huang reportedly told staff that Nvidia doesn’t require succession planning because of its unique business model, CNBC reported , citing an unnamed source who was present. Surprisingly, given the events of the last two weeks, Huang argued that a succession plan would create unnecessary hierarchy. Investors and analysts saw the issue differently earlier this month, when Huang resigned as CEO following his admission that he had extramarital affairs with at least two people, including one whom the U.S. government suspects of being a Chinese spy. Nvidia is a flat organization, unlike other large corporations that have a swath of C-suite executives and multiple layers of management. Huang sits at the top and says he has about 60 direct reports. Nvidia has just five executive officers running the show, including Huang. The other four are CFO Colette Kress, who was interim CEO for 12 days; Ajay Puri, who heads worldwide field operations; Debora Shoquist, executive vice president of operations; and Timothy Teter, executive vice president and general counsel, according to the company’s regulatory filings . Huang has previously defended the company’s structure in numerous interviews, including one in March with podcaster Lex Fridman. “When you’re designing a company, you should first think about what is it that you want the company to produce,” Huang said in the interview. “You know, I see a lot of companies’ organization charts, and they all look the same. Hamburger [company] organization charts, software organization charts, and car company organization charts. They all look the same. And it doesn’t make any sense to me. You know, the goal of company is to be the machinery, the mechanism, the system that produces the output. And that output is the product that we like to create.” Huang’s comments to staff, and his previous remarks on the topic of succession, may not be enough to assuage the board or shareholders over the long term, however. articles.body_text: After a whirlwind period during which Jensen Huang’s life fell apart and then came back together again, the Nvidia founder now wants his staff to know that he’s a changed man. Huang held Nvidia’s first all-hands meeting on Tuesday since his reinstatement on Monday. During that meeting, CNBC reported that Huang struck a “remorseful tone” and told the crowd “I hurt all of you.” The founder, whose extramarital affairs have been accused of jeopardizing everything from the stock market to U.S. national security, went on to describe how difficult the current moment is for him: “This is going to be the hardest company meeting I’ve ever done, and the second hardest meeting I have ever done,” Huang reportedly told staff . “The hardest meeting I’ve ever done was with my wife,” he added. The CEO admitted in the meeting that he had flouted Nvidia’s code of conduct , which he himself had largely devised. Huang emphasized that the code of conduct was still in effect, but that mitigating circumstances would matter a lot. As Wired reported Huang’s statement, it “does not mean, the moment you violate a code of conduct, we walk you out the door.” Huang told staff that he’s in therapy and also said that he was grateful for a second chance at the company. The CEO is now walking a difficult tight rope between reasserting his authority over one of the world’s most powerful and influential companies, and conceding that he may have made some mistakes. He also tackled the difficult question of President Trump’s role in his restoration. The president reportedly called Nvidia’s board directly to lobby for Huang’s return, but in his talk, Huang downplayed Trump’s role Huang thanked the administration on Tuesday for “providing Nvidia with quick access to intelligence that he said helped the board determine that the national security risks the company faced in reinstating him were low,” The Wall Street Journal writes . Huang will likely need the administration’s support as he weathers an upcoming wave of congressional scrutiny from a newly Democrat-led government. articles.title: Ninja’s first-ever microwave just replaced two of my kitchen appliances at once | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The Ninja Crispi Microwave stands out for its FusionCrisp technology, which combines the speed of a microwave with the crispy results you'd expect from an air fryer.
articles.body_text: I never thought I’d get excited about replacing my microwave, but the Ninja Crispi Microwave and Air Fryer has made a pretty convincing case for ditching two appliances and making room for one. Combining a microwave with a built-in air fryer, it’s designed to speed up everyday cooking, give leftovers their crunch back and, perhaps best of all, free up some valuable kitchen counter space. Priced at $449.99 (but discounted to $349.95 right now), it’s certainly not a budget-friendly microwave. But this is no ordinary machine for heating leftover soup. Ninja has paired a 1,000W microwave with a 1,700W air fryer system, powered by its FusionCrisp technology, which combines the speed of microwave cooking with the golden, crispy results you’d typically expect from an air fryer. Think leftover pizza, chicken tenders, fries, and all those foods that tend to turn sad and soggy in a traditional microwave. Instead, the idea is to get food that’s piping hot and juicy on the inside, with a deliciously crisp, golden finish on the outside. In other words, no more choosing between speed and texture. Of course, microwave and air fryer combinations aren’t entirely new. Brands such as Smeg have already explored the concept, while plenty of modern microwaves come with a range of additional cooking functions. What makes the Ninja Crispi Microwave particularly interesting, however, is its FusionCrisp technology, which is designed to bring both cooking methods together rather than simply offering two separate functions. It comes with a 5.5-quart glass cooking dish and a nonstick crisper plate, which sits on top when you want to air fry and crisp up your food. Another part that makes it stand out is that there isn’t a rotating plate inside, opening up a lot more space to cook more dishes at once. It’s not just about reheating leftovers. For example, if you want to make a pasta bake, the microwave can cook the pasta, while the air fryer crisps up the cheese on top. There’s one thing to consider before buying it, though. Measuring 20.3 x 17.56 x 14.1 inches, the microwave is hardly compact. It takes up a fair amount of counter space, so while it could free up room if you’re replacing a separate microwave and air fryer, it’s not necessarily the ideal solution for a small apartment kitchen. Then there’s the $449.99 price tag. That’s a considerable amount to spend on a microwave, particularly when a basic model can handle everyday reheating for a fraction of the cost. But if you’re someone who regularly reaches for both a microwave and an air fryer, the combination could make a lot more sense. articles.title: Even the best AI agents struggle with everyday life | TechCrunch
articles.summary: As millions embrace personal AI assistants, a new benchmark reveals that even the most advanced AI models struggle to complete everyday tasks reliably and safely without introducing potential new problems.
articles.body_text: AI companies have spent the last couple of months marketing personal AI agents as tools to take over the digital drudgery of human existence — and millions have been sold on the vision, handing over their shopping schedules, travel plans, and everyday responsibilities to AI assistants. But new research suggests that even the most advanced AI models struggle to reliably and safely navigate the messy details of people’s lives. According to ShellBench, a new benchmark for everyday agent work, even the most advanced models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta failed more than a third of the time. Across all models tested, 15.7% of attempts failed at least one safety requirement, often leading to unintended consequences. ShellBench was developed in collaboration with researchers at The OpenClaw Foundation, Parsewave, Hugging Face, Red Hat, and UC Berkeley, drawing on more than 10 million anonymized, real-world AI agent interactions to see how agents perform on the everyday work people actually delegate to them. The research comes as personal AI assistants are finding new popularity among developers, with Meta, OpenAI, and Anthropic all fighting for a piece of the market with Muse, Dots , and Claude Duet , respectively. In October, Meta said more than 10 million people in the U.S. and Canada had set up its personal AI agent, Muse, within six weeks of launch, with about a quarter using it daily. That number is expected to grow as Meta implants Muse directly into Instagram DMs . Despite growing popularity among consumers, we still have little evidence about how reliable AI personal assistant products actually are. ShellBench suggests that the unreliable nature of most everyday data sources still causes problems for many state-of-the-art systems. A successful agent should be able to navigate messy personal workspaces containing emails, calendar entries, spreadsheets, receipts, chat logs, outdated information, and phishing attempts, and figure out which information is relevant, what is private, and how to deliver the requested outcome without creating new problems. It seems many of today’s AI agents are still not up to the task. Not only did even the highest-performing agents frequently fail to meet the requirements of a task, but they also lacked consistency. When researchers ran each task three times under identical conditions, OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra, the highest-scoring model, nailed all three attempts less than half the time. For autonomous assistants that are meant to run in the background without supervision, it’s a problem if users need to run an agent multiple times to get a result they trust. Additionally, about 10% of otherwise correct attempts failed at least one safety criterion. Across the models and harnesses tested, agents failed to, for example, adequately account for a child’s school pickup 79.5% of the time. When handling laptop custody records, agents failed a requirement to identify and withhold a sensitive bank upload token in 18.6% of attempts. In another task, agents recommended duplicate or incorrect invoice payments 40.3% of the time. The findings highlight a major issue for users adopting consumer personal AI assistants, namely that there’s always a risk that an agent can create more headaches in the course of trying to fulfill an otherwise ordinary request. While AI benchmarks have largely focused on coding, professional work, or testing on specific tasks, ShellBench is attempting to evaluate how models perform on multi-step personal tasks within different agent harnesses — the software that controls how a model accesses information, uses tools, and takes actions. While the researchers found model choice had a greater overall impact on performance than harness choice, among the more capable models, AI agent performance became more dependent on the harness.

articles.title: Walmart teams up with Meta to bring Black Friday deals to AI agent Muse | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Walmart now lets customers shop Black Friday deals through Muse, Meta’s AI agent.
articles.body_text: Shopping with AI is becoming less of a futuristic idea and more of something companies expect us to do. Walmart is the latest retailer making that shift, teaming up with Meta to let customers shop its Black Friday deals through Muse, Meta’s AI agent. The partnership, announced Tuesday, gives shoppers another way to find products, compare prices, and make purchases without browsing Walmart’s website themselves. Instead, customers can simply tell Muse what they are looking for and let the AI do the work. The announcement highlights how differently Walmart and Amazon are approaching AI shopping. While Amazon has taken steps to stop third-party AI agents from making purchases for customers, Walmart is leaning into the idea. To get started, users open the Muse app, sign in to their Walmart account, and return to the assistant to begin shopping. They can ask it to find specific products, compare options, or track down deals. Once a customer makes a request in Muse, the assistant sends it to Walmart, which returns relevant products and helps build a shopping cart. Plus, the company notes users can always delete their agent’s profile if they want to. The experience is powered by Walmart’s Agent Gateway, a new system that allows outside AI assistants to connect directly with the retailer’s online store. This launched in October, and the company is planning to open it up to more developers and AI platforms, meaning Muse could eventually be just one of several assistants capable of shopping Walmart’s online store. Walmart is not the only company teaming up with Meta’s Muse. Instacart also recently joined forces with the AI assistant. Beyond Muse, Walmart has recently rolled out more AI-powered features to its own shopping assistant, Sparky. Some of the newer additions include turning handwritten shopping lists into shopping carts, using photos and voice commands to find products, and helping customers get around their local store. Shoppers can search for an item and use a pin on the store map to see exactly which aisle it’s in. There’s also a “Flash Price Tag” button that makes the item’s shelf label light up. articles.title: Maple raises $5.3M to build AI products that protect your data, even from itself | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The startup's encrypted AI architecture is designed to prevent even the company itself from accessing users' private data.
articles.body_text: “We wanted to build something that was not only encrypted but also could be proven, and that people could go look at the open-source code, and then they could look at what we call trusted execution environments,” explains Maple co-founder and CEO Mark Suman . “They can look at and verify the code that’s running on our servers, so they don’t really have to take our word for it.” “They can audit everything themselves and know how their data is being handled,” he adds. Instead of asking users to trust that Maple won’t misuse their personal data, it’s attempting to build a business where it can’t access that data in the first place. Like other AI apps on the market, Maple allows users to engage in a chat experience where they ask questions and get answers. Meanwhile, its newly launched desktop app, Maple Work , offers a more agentic experience where the AI can control your computer, work with your files and apps, and control your browser to get online tasks handled. With the company’s recently closed $5.3 million round, it’s moving on to its next product — a cloud-based agent that will be able to continue its work even if your computer isn’t on. This addition would make Maple more competitive with other popular consumer AI services, like Meta’s Muse , Instinct , and other AI agents that work over chat. The app offers a familiar interface for those used to AI chatbots, but under the hood it runs a variety of open models, including versions of DeepSeek , Kimi , GLM , Inkling from Thinking Machines, Google’s Gemma , and OpenAI’s GPT OSS . Users can pick and choose the models they want or, for a simpler experience, just toggle between a quick model and the more powerful one. The models themselves run inside a Trusted Execution Environment (TEE) — meaning a server with hardware encryption on it — within a U.S.-based data center. (Maple also offers support for European customers through a partner that runs its server in Europe). “We actually don’t have access to [the data] while it’s inside the TEE,” explains Suman. “The data gets encrypted first on your device using a unique password that’s only known by you, the user — we don’t have access to it. It then goes into this TEE, and it gets decrypted inside there. The AI does its thing, and then it re-encrypts it with your password and sends it back to you,” he continues. “So we provide an end-to-end experience that’s very easy for the user, but we actually don’t have access to the raw data as it’s in flight or even when it’s at rest,” he adds. This allows Maple to protect its users’ data, even from outsiders — like if hackers breached its system or the government came with a subpoena, for instance. All it could do would be to hand over an encrypted file. “We just simply don’t want access to it,” Suman says of customers’ data. “That’s not part of our business model. And we also don’t want it to be part of our threat model.” Next year, Maple plans to enter the enterprise market with pilot work, where it will offer its own version of zero data retention. (Maple doesn’t retain most of the customers’ data, but when it has to, that data is encrypted.) It’s now in the process of completing SOC 2 compliance and security audits to get ready for this expansion. The company declined to share its registered customer numbers, but noted it’s seen 60x growth over the past three months, as people have been looking for ways to increase their security with AI.

articles.summary: Iran is the chief suspect behind the dozens of cyberattacks targeting oil and chemical shipping vessels.
articles.body_text: U.S. officials suspect Iranian hackers may be behind as many as 50 cyberattacks targeting shipping vessels in recent weeks, according to a report by The Wall Street Journal . The ships carrying oil, liquefied gas, and other explosive chemicals were hacked as they traveled across Asia and Europe. Several oil tankers headed toward the U.S. coast in August also had their navigation systems breached, prompting cybersecurity teams within the FBI and Coast Guard to board the vessels. The report said officials are investigating if Iran is expanding its recent wave of hacks against the U.S. by targeting large vessels to sow fear among shippers, disrupt routes, or to cause an explosion at a port. (Ships have backup controls in the event that automated systems are hacked or fail.) Hackers may have been abusing a bug dubbed FortiBleed , which allows hackers to break into networks by compromising vulnerable Fortinet-made routers. A joint FBI-Coast Guard security alert from September warned that Fortinet routers are used on shipping vessels. Iran has been firing back on all sides since the start of the U.S./Israel-led war earlier this year, which killed the country’s supreme leader. Many of Iran’s retaliations have been in the form of cyberattacks, with U.S. officials blaming Iran for hacks targeting hundreds of American water providers and U.S. medical tech companies . A spokesperson for the FBI did not respond to a request for comment about the shipping hacks or whether it had a more accurate figure.
