articles.title: Anthropic shares fall below IPO price, a worrying sign for AI startups | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Anthropic’s post-IPO slump could put pressure on AI startup valuations.
articles.body_text: Anthropic’s stock fell below its IPO price of $83 , trading as low as $76 a share by midday Tuesday, down nearly 12% from Monday’s close. Falling below the IPO price is often seen as a negative signal because underwriters typically price offerings at a discount to their expected trading value. The AI industry has been eagerly watching how Anthropic’s shares trade, with VCs and other observers saying its performance could serve as a barometer for how public market investors value the sector. The dramatic slump comes less than a week after Anthropic debuted on Nasdaq at $111.50 a share . If its shares continue to trade poorly in the coming weeks, the slide could put pressure on private startup valuations and weaken IPO prospects for other AI companies. Anthropic isn’t the only AI stock selling off on Tuesday. Nvidia fell more than 7% by midday, giving back some of the more than 30%-plus gain it posted Monday after Jensen Huang was reinstated as CEO. articles.title: Why a Crusoe investor is betting on solar and batteries to power future AI data centers | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Next-generation data centers will need tens of gigawatts of power every year. One of Crusoe's investors thinks solar and energy storage are the obvious choice.
articles.body_text: The problem of supplying power to AI data centers has become one of the central debates of the AI era. In just a few years, the U.S. grid has gone from basically zero growth to adding several gigawatts a year. “Demand is growing faster than people appreciate,” Brook Porter, partner at G2 Venture Partners (G2VP), told TechCrunch. “It’s atoms, not bits, and the world is in the process of recognizing the realities of those challenges.” It’s been a bumpy road. Because it takes a while to scale supply chains, companies have been securing power in any form they can. In many cases, that has meant buying, renting, and deploying natural gas power plants , but Porter thinks that hyperscalers and data center developers should look at the bigger picture if they want to move faster. That picture involves solar paired with energy storage, based on an analysis Porter and his colleagues at G2VP recently conducted on the state of the data center power market. “Global capacity of natural gas is only about 60 or 70 gigawatts per year, where solar is already at well over a terawatt,” he said. “Probably the most important lesson that we’ve learned over the last 20 years of backing companies is that Wright’s Law is the thing you want to leverage — making the same thing over and over again.” Both solar and most forms of long-duration energy storage are built on small, modular technologies that can be manufactured at massive scale. “This is about speed and scale and economics, and we can win across all those dimensions,” Porter said. G2VP had an early window into AI data center development, having led Crusoe’s Series C . “We’ve had a front-row seat at what’s been happening at that company, how they’ve evolved, how the different waves of data centers have evolved,” Porter said. The venture firm estimates that data center investment will top $4 trillion until the end of the decade. As the next wave takes shape, the firm sees two different paths for data centers: small, on-grid facilities with their own generating capacity, and larger data centers powered by solar and long-duration energy storage. “The big idea is to go off-grid,” Porter said. “What that would enable you to do is build with renewables in a way that’s independent of the grid. You can determine your own fate, go around some of the constraints of permitting, whether that’s access to the grid or air permits. You can accelerate your time to market dramatically.” In recent years, energy storage has been synonymous with lithium-ion batteries, which are too expensive to compete with fossil fuels for round-the-clock power. But a new generation of long-duration energy storage products from the likes of Form Energy and G2VP portfolio company Antora Energy have brought the cost per megawatt-hour down significantly. Even though the technologies might be a few years away from broad acceptance among data center developers, Porter said they should start thinking about them now. “It’s analogous to surfing the biggest waves off of Mavericks here in Northern California. The wave is so big that you really have to be paddling and moving and be incredibly nimble to catch it. If you’re at a standstill, it’s just gonna blow you by,” he said.

articles.title: Amazon's Decart acquisition is a bet on using software to narrow the silicon gap with Nvidia | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Amazon’s decision to acquire Decart for a reported $7.5 billion is part of its efforts to improve the efficiency of its Trainium chips.
articles.body_text: Jensen Huang’s comeback as Nvidia’s CEO is understandably making waves, leaving people wondering about the longer-term implications of his quick reinstatement and the U.S. government’s active role in his return. But there was another development yesterday that could also matter for Nvidia down the road: Amazon’s decision to acquire Decart ‘s tech and its team for a reported $7.5 billion . The broader industry seems to agree that Decart’s tech for optimizing AI models to run on non-Nvidia chips is worth several billion dollars. Anthropic reportedly tried to acquire the startup in the same ballpark , and Nvidia, which invested in the startup’s $300 million funding round at a $4 billion valuation , was also rumored as a prospective buyer. Amazon was ultimately the one to pull the trigger and bring on board Decart’s co-founders Dean Leitersdorf, Orian Leitersdorf, and Moshe Shalev and their team , but the company is not interested in the world models they had been working on . At the heart of the deal is the startup’s tech that helps AI models run better on all kinds of chips. By incorporating the startup’s Decart Optimization Stack (DOS), Amazon is now hoping to extract more performance out of its Trainium chips, as the company tries to turn AWS into a $1 trillion revenue business . In its announcement , Amazon said it has worked with Decart since 2025 to optimize the Trainium chips. This deal is ostensibly aimed at accelerating that work, which could eventually result in the company offering its Trainium-based data centers, which Anthropic already uses, to more customers. Amazon has already been working to make Trainium easier to switch to . One way Nvidia managed to leapfrog its competitors was by spending $6.9 billion to acquire Israeli chipmaker Mellanox, which eventually grew to become a core piece of its international manufacturing strategy . Amazon could well be following a similar path. Annapurna Labs makes for a more interesting parallel than Mellanox, however, as the latter formed the basis of Amazon’s custom chip-designing unit following its 2015 acquisition . Add Intel into the mix , and this becomes a broader story. “Most of the hardware powering the AI wave was built in Israel. Annapurna; Mellanox; Habana Labs; etc…,” VC Eric Reiner observed on X a few months ago. In an email to TechCrunch, Eze Vidra, co-founder and managing partner at Remagine Ventures, said the deal is “a strong signal for the Israeli deep-tech ecosystem, showing that specialized local talent continues to attract major global players.” Amazon still has a ways to go before it can make a dent in Nvidia’s near-monopoly on AI chips, but the deal could help the e-commerce giant speed up its efforts. Dean Meyer, a partner at Sequoia who co-led the firm’s seed investment into Decart, said on X that the deal “will be looked back on as one of the most strategically important acquisitions in many, many years.” When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission . articles.title: Nintendo Switch Online’s N64 and Sega Genesis ‘expansion pack’ launches October 25th for $49.99 per year
articles.summary: Nintendo has announced the pricing for its Switch Online + Expansion Pack subscription service: it’ll cost $49.99 per year for a single subscription, or $79.99 for a family membership. In addition to N64 and Genesis games, it’ll also include access to the new paid Animal Crossing DLC.
articles.body_text: Nintendo has announced the price and release for its upcoming Nintendo Switch Online + Expansion Pack subscription tier, which adds Nintendo 64 games, Sega Genesis games, and bundled access to the new paid Animal Crossing: New Horizons — Happy Home Paradise DLC. It’ll cost $49.99 per year for an individual subscription or $79.99 for a shared family membership. The service will officially launch on October 25th. Those prices are a big jump from the regular Switch Online subscription, which costs $19.99 per year for a single membership or $34.99 per year for a family subscription. The Nintendo Switch Online + Expansion Pack subscription tier offers the same benefits as the standard Switch Online service — including online multiplayer, classic NES and SNES games, cloud saves, and other perks. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/22929332/Screen_Shot_2021_10_15_at_10.32.07_AM.png?quality=90&strip=all] But the Expansion Pack subscription also adds access to other retro titles from the Nintendo 64 and Sega Genesis. Today’s pricing announcement included news that the premium subscription service would also bring bundled access to the new paid Animal Crossing: New Horizons DLC (which is set to cost $24.99 on its own). At launch, the Nintendo Switch Online + Expansion Pack service will include several of the most popular N64 games, including Super Mario 64, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, and Mario Kart 64. Additional titles are also planned for the future, like Banjo-Kazooie, Pokémon Snap, The Legend of Zelda: Majora’s Mask, and Paper Mario. The higher $49.99 per year price point also puts Nintendo Switch Online + Expansion Pack more in line with other major subscription costs from competitors like Sony and Microsoft (PlayStation Plus and Xbox Live Gold both cost $59.99 per year, albeit with fewer perks than Nintendo’s retro game offerings). In addition to the Switch Online + Expansion Pack details, Nintendo also opened preorders for the matching wireless Nintendo 64 and Sega Genesis controllers (each $49.99, with USB-C charging) that its selling to go with the new retro games. The new controllers are set to ship alongside the new service on October 25th. Update October 15th, 10:44AM ET: Added release date information. articles.title: Twitter makes stock symbol $ ‘cashtag’ links official, following # and @
articles.summary: Now another common standard will automatically be turned into links when viewed on Twitter.com - $ stock symbols. Twitter announced it in a tweet that indeed contains a stock link that is clickable on the web, much as it has been on various Twitter clients before today. Clicking on a ticker link takes you to a straight Twitter search for the symbol.
articles.body_text: Twitter has a long history of letting its users create standards and then finally adopting them as site features. First came the @ reply, whose history was recently examined. Next, the # hashtag morphed into Twitter’s full “Discover” tab — complete with advertising opportunities. Now another common standard will automatically be turned into links when viewed on Twitter.com - $ stock symbols, commonly referred to as “cashtags.” Twitter announced it in a tweet that indeed contains a stock link that is clickable on the web, much as it has been on various Twitter clients before today. Clicking on a ticker link takes you to a straight Twitter search for the symbol. Twitter has been working to make its website better at showing related information in “expanded Tweets” that, in part, make it so a user doesn’t need to leave Twitter.com. While the tweets with stock ticker symbols don’t yet show expanded information, we imagine that it’s an obvious opportunity to do so.

Steven Spielberg’s Ready Player One improves immensely on the book
articles.summary: Ernest Cline’s fast-moving, bestselling novel was a treasure trove for pop-culture junkies. But the endless references to video games and movies work better on the screen, where most of them originated in the first place.
articles.body_text: Fans tend to either love or hate Ernest Cline’s bestselling 2011 novel Ready Player One. There are legitimate reasons for both reactions. On the love side: it’s a light, airy pop confection, crammed with familiar cultural references, which Cline recontextualizes in surprising ways. On the hate side: the prose can be extremely clumsy, as it is in this paragraph where teenage protagonist Wade Watts describes the virtual car he constructed for himself in the vast online world where he spends most of his waking hours: > The DeLorean came outfitted with a (nonfunctioning) flux capacitor, but I’d made several additions to its equipment and appearance. First, I’d installed an artificially intelligent onboard computer named KITT (purchased in an online auction) into the dashboard, along with a matching red Knight Rider scanner just above the DeLorean’s grill. Then I’d outfitted the car with an oscillation overthruster, a device that allowed it to travel through solid matter. Finally, to complete my ‘80s super-vehicle theme, I’d slapped a Ghostbusters logo on each of the DeLorean’s gull-wing doors, then added personalized plates that read ECTO-88. That’s a lot of awkward verbiage to say two pretty basic things: people in virtual reality can express their personal tastes through their avatars in hyper-specific ways, and Cline is so obsessed with the culture of the 1980s — the geek-fodder of his youth — that he thinks it’s compelling even in the form of a shopping list. The book is a fast-paced adventure, but this kind of unwieldy lump of mix-and-match nostalgia acts as a roadblock. There’s no attempt to consider why Wade finds these specific objects appealing, out of the billion options available to him. The book assumes up front that readers find everything in this list as unbearably cool as Cline does, and that just running down an exhaustive list of Wade’s favorite things is enough to make him appealing, relatable, and enviable. Steven Spielberg’s new film adaptation of Ready Player One prominently features that same car, but in a context that improves it immensely. Spielberg doesn’t have Wade talk audiences through it, and he doesn’t spell out the references. He just slaps the car down in the middle of a tremendous early action scene, where it’s prominent, distinctive, and memorable. Fans who want the full nostalgia trip, who want to wring every Easter egg out of the experience, will eventually be able to pause the movie and frame-by-frame through it, looking for the flux capacitor on the dashboard, checking the plates, and scanning for extra bonus material. But in the middle of the action, even to people who’ve never seen the Back to the Future movies and aren’t vibing on the connection, the car doesn’t need explaining. It’s just a sleek piece of visual energy, one breathless element among dozens of others. It’s not a citation or a list. It’s an effortless, integrated piece of the action. [Media: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cSp1dM2Vj48] That dynamic stretches throughout Ready Player One, scripted by Cline and X-Men: The Last Stand writer Zak Penn, and directed by Spielberg as a whiplash-fast tear through a world-spanning, all-encompassing video game. The story, which mostly takes place in the virtual-reality world called The OASIS, rarely slows down enough to explain the references, or geek out over them the way the book does. It’s still a visual festival of ‘80s culture that sometimes hinges significant jokes on the assumption that the audience knows the filmography of Robert Zemeckis, or will chortle over a reference to Monty Python and the Holy Grail. But the film improves significantly on the book by prioritizing the story over the signifiers. The hardcore pop-culture crowd that is this movie’s ultimate intended audience will have plenty to pore over and pick apart in this film. But the story moves briskly enough, and with enough giant-sized, screen-friendly excitement, that it doesn’t feel like it’s aimed solely and specifically at them. Some of that speed comes at the expense of artistry. Ready Player One opens by laboriously climbing a mountain of voiceover, explaining the setting: the year is 2045, and the world is terrible. Most people live in depressing poverty, and spend as much time as possible jacked into the fantasy world of the OASIS. There, they can be and do anything they want, or at least anything they can afford to buy with coins won in the universe’s eternally running video game arenas. The OASIS was created by reclusive genius James Halliday (Bridge of Spies’ Mark Rylance), who packed it with his own favorite culture. When he died, he created a three-part quest within the world, linked to his favorite films and games, but also tied to his own past regrets and frustrations. Whoever finds the three keys he’s hidden within the game world, and the ultimate Easter egg they unlock, will get full control of OASIS and Halliday’s vast fortune. The quest has created a subclass of “egg-hunters,” or “Gunters” — quest-obsessives whose full-time occupation is hunting down the keys. It’s also created an evil dystopian megacorp, run by former Halliday intern Nolan Sorrento (Ben Mendelsohn, of Rogue One and Starred Up), and devoted to gaining control of the OASIS to commercialize it. Wade (X-Men: Apocalypse’s Tye Sheridan) and his fellow Gunters — particularly too-cool-for-school solo hunter Art3mis (Olivia Cooke, also currently starring in the chilling Thoroughbreds) and Wade’s big mechanical buddy Aech (Master of None’s Lena Waithe) — all want the keys and the egg for their own personal reasons, though those are barely articulated. Cline’s book assumes everyone will know a DeLorean is cool; Spielberg’s film assumes the same thing about a teenage protagonist who loves playing video games. Wade (or Parzival, as he’s known in the OASIS) eventually develops an ethos, but for the most part, he’s like every other video gamer who’s ever sat down on a couch and hit “start” on the controller. He may appreciate the gameplay or the storyline or the people he meets online, but ultimately, he just wants that elusive win. He’s more a customized audience avatar than a real character, but that’s fitting for a world that’s so spottily drawn, at least outside of the virtual paradise where people prefer to spent their time. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/9820163/29ed3d416cd513893ea80d1e6c9a560e.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] The film version of Ready Player One has some major advantages over the book. The exposition is just as bald, but once it’s done, Spielberg can focus on the endless dynamism of a world where anything is possible. As Wade and others follow their quest through races, battles, and puzzles, they encounter a dizzying blur of visual references that act as “Hey, remember this?” in-jokes with the audience, including some major ones that weren’t in the book. But the filmmakers also delve into Halliday’s past and his wounded psyche, in a way that gradually becomes a little touching and tragic. (A conversation with Halliday’s online avatar closely recalls a similar scene with Professor Falken in WarGames, and carries the same sense of melancholy.) The film also goes further than the book in laying out why Halliday’s retreat into a fantasy world wasn’t necessarily good for anyone — especially not for Halliday himself. No matter how validating the onscreen gags are, they’re still a reminder of a man who found more emotional resonance in Jurassic Park’s T-Rex than in a connection with a living human being. The film inevitably has its cake and eats it too when it comes to addressing wish-fulfillment fantasy and delirious nostalgia: the story can only push so far in sorrowing over Halliday’s surrender and retreat from the world, while still turning every rambunctious game setpiece into a celebration of Cline’s favorite culture. Ready Player One is so heavily inspired by and inflected with the broad, black-and-white morality of ‘80s geek culture that any attempt to find the gray areas feels slightly daring, even as it feels slightly out of place. Given that Sorrento is a buttoned-down, stony-faced idea-thief of an evil overlord, straight out of Tron, there’s not a lot of room for narrative nuance in this story. But at least Cline and Penn make the effort, acknowledging some of the biggest complaints leveled at Cline’s book, and trying to take the story a little deeper. The film version does carry over some of the book’s most notable flaws, especially a suspicious reliance on narrative convenience and coincidence. The characters are thinly drawn, and most of them are little more than cool avatars and signature moves. There’s no sense that anyone involved with the story really cares about the details of the real world in this crapsack future, given how little the real-world scenes hold together. And the film takes a particularly feather-light approach to what should be significant emotions, especially when a death that should devastate Wade is shrugged off within seconds, then brought back out for a cheap, unearned moment much later. Spielberg’s signature sentiment is operating in full force, as he builds up one highly symbolic confrontation solely for the feelings of triumph and justice it creates, and then has it come to exactly nothing. And in places, the story jumps forward so quickly that it feels like necessary connective scenes are simply missing. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/10408527/ready_player_one.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] Unequivocally, the film’s biggest problem is the half-assed love story between Wade and Art3mis, which operates on approximately 75 percent wish-fulfillment and 25 percent apathetic inevitability. When they first encounter each other, Wade is starstruck: he knows Art3mis from her online cool-girl rep, and watching her in action, he sees her as an über-badass with leet skillz and an appealingly punk devil-may-care attitude. It’s a short, shocking jump from there to him telling her he loves her. What follows should be important and telling — she reminds him that they don’t know each other, that he’s seeing an online avatar and a mental picture he’s largely invented. (And, of course, he thinks they’re perfect for each other because she gets his references.) But the film never follows through on that mature and useful point. The insta-relationship that develops between them is as inauthentic and insulting as the central romance in Edgar Wright’s Scott Pilgrim Vs. The World, without any of the sense of irony or intentionality. It’s bad enough to follow the “hero wins the girl as a prize” model without examining it at all. It’s worse still to have the characters examine it, find the flaws, then instantly forget about them. This isn’t a movie with a long memory (except when it’s reaching back 40 years for visual gags), but it’s infuriating to see it try to examine its own tropes responsibly, then take no steps whatsoever to address the issues it raises. And yet, when Wade is in his kitted-out DeLorean, tearing along a preposterously difficult game racetrack, menaced by King Kong and dodging flying debris as his fellow racers crash and burn, very little of that matters. The sheer dynamism and energy of the movie are compelling, even when the character drama isn’t. The action scenes are deliberately overclocked and overwhelming, turning Wade’s quest into a thrilling blur of fast-paced decisions and the endorphin-rush highs of a good gaming experience. More importantly, the film is overtly funny in ways that constantly remind the audience that there are people behind the game avatars, and specifically people who are sometimes young, self-absorbed, immature, and caught up in their own created self-images of badassery. The human frailties behind the game avatars is a reliable well of humor for Ready Player One, and the script takes full, hilarious advantage. And while the film’s real world gets left behind in the rush, the attention to detail during the OASIS scenes is absolutely astounding — not just the details Cline salivated over on the page, like that Knight Rider scanner in the grill of Wade’s car, but the subtle nuances, like the way Wade’s avatar constantly seems to be standing in a flattering breeze that ruffles his hair in the most winsome way possible, or the way Art3mis’ too-big anime eyes catch the light. The uncanny-valley effect is strong in these game avatars, but Spielberg uses it to his advantage, reminding his audience at every moment that what they’re seeing is mostly a fantasy, created by people who see image as almost everything. It’s a slick, sleek, surface fantasy, for sure. But for people who share Cline’s worldview, or identify with gamer culture in general, it’s an immense hit of validation and acknowledgement, delivered with joyful abandon and unmissable enthusiasm. All those feelings of love and obsession came through clearly on the page. But on the screen, they’re bigger and better, because they’re so much more intense, and so much closer to the memorable images that turned Cline into an obsessive in the first place. This review was initially published after Ready Player One’s premiere at the 2018 SXSW festival in Austin, Texas. The film arrives in theaters on March 29th, 2018.

articles.title: JUST NU: C:s vägval: Höger eller extra val
articles.summary: Centerpartiets ledning ser bara två vägar framåt. Antingen tar man plats i en högerregering – eller så blir det extraval där C får skulden för kaoset i regeringsbildningsprocessen. articles.body_text: Centerpartiets ledning ser bara två vägar framåt. Antingen tar man plats i en högerregering – eller så blir det extraval där C får skulden för kaoset i regeringsbildningsprocessen. På internmötet ska Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist ha sagt att C nu ”tar stryk” av att partiet är ”bråkiga”, uppger personer som var med på mötet för Expressen. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. På tisdagskvällen träffades stora delar av Centerpartiets toppskikt och systerorganisationer på ett digitalt informationsmöte. Över 500 personer deltog. Expressen har pratat med flera mötesdeltagare. Rubriken var ”lägesuppdatering i förhandlingarna” och under mötet berättade Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist, Ulrika Heie, Rickard Nordin och partisekreterare Hannes Hervieu om att man inte fattat något formellt beslut om vägen framåt än, och att man nu noggrannare tittar på innehållet i Moderaternas totalpaket. Men samtidigt ska det ha framgått tydligt att ledningen bara ser två möjliga vägar framåt efter att förhandlingarna om en rödgrön regering misslyckats. Antingen tar Centerpartiet plats i en högerregering som leds av Ulf Kristersson. Hannes Hervieu ska på mötet sagt att partiets väljare föredrar att man hittar en lösning på situationen snarare än går till extraval, enligt Expressens uppgifter. Om det blir extraval skulle Centerpartiet straffas av väljarna, ska även partiledare Thand Ringqvist ha uttryckt tydligt och tillagt att partiet just nu ”tar stryk” för att man upplevs som ”bråkiga i regeringsförhandlingarna”. Hon ska också ha sagt att man räknar med att det blir svårt för partiet att få genomslag i ett eventuellt extraval eftersom C kommer få mycket av skulden för de nuvarande förhandlingarna, uppger en person som var med på mötet. Thand Ringqvist ska även ha berättat om hur man försökt samtala med Vänsterpartiet på olika nivåer.

articles.title: Trebarnsmamman dödad av flera djur
articles.summary: Allison Anderson skulle snart bli mormor för första gången. Då blev 36-åriga trebarnsmamman dödad av hundar.
articles.body_text: Allison Anderson skulle snart bli mormor för första gången. Då blev 36-åriga trebarnsmamman dödad av hundar, skriver NBC News . – Jag är så äcklad att ägarna till dessa hundar inte hade kontroll över dem, säger dottern Miley Garner. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. 36-åriga Allison Anderson, som var trebarnsmamma och arméveteran, hittades förra veckan död på gården intill ett hus i en småstad utanför Atlanta, USA . Preliminära obduktionsresultat tyder på Anderson fick dödliga skador efter att ha ”blivit attackerad av hundar”, enligt polisen. ”Flera av hundarna som var inblandade i attacken har lokaliserats och är i förvar”, skriver polisen. Andersons dotter Miley Garner sade att hennes mamma dog innan hon hann berätta för henne att hon skulle bli mormor för första gången. – Om min mamma visste att jag bär på hennes första barnbarn skulle hon vara överlycklig och upprymd. Jag är så äcklad och fullständigt förkrossad över att ägarna till dessa hundar inte hade kontroll över dem. Det min mamma gick igenom var tortyr, säger Garner. Andersons systerdotter Samantha Evans berättade för NBC News att de fortfarande håller på att bearbeta ”detta fruktansvärda brott”. – Min moster skulle precis bli mormor för första gången när hon dödades. Vi vill ha rättvisa, säger Evans. Ingen har gripits i samband med Andersons död.

articles.title: Rådet till Mette-Marit: Prata inte om Epstein
articles.summary: Norges drottning Mette-Marit kommer inte att ställa upp på ett samtal med den norska Epstein-kommissionen. Hovet har avböjt förfrågan efter en rekommendation från statsministerns kansli
articles.body_text: Norges drottning Mette-Marit kommer inte att ställa upp på ett samtal med den norska Epstein-kommissionen. Hovet har avböjt förfrågan efter en rekommendation från statsministerns kansli, rapporterar NRK . Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Det stormade rejält i Norge när Epsteinfilerna offentliggjordes i början av året. Dokumenten visade att flera norska toppnamn, bland dem den dåvarande kronprinsessan Mette-Marit och tidigare statsministern Thorbjørn Jagland, hade haft tät kontakt med den dömde sexualförbrytaren Jeffrey Epstein, som dog i häkte 2019. I april beslutade därför stortinget att tillsätta en oberoende granskningskommission med uppdrag att kartlägga kontakterna och utreda om de har äventyrat landets säkerhet. Men något samtal med Mette-Marit, som i dag är landets drottning, blir det inte. När kommissionen i oktober bjöd in drottningen till ett samtal tackade hovet nej, rapporterar NRK. Korrespondens som NRK har tagit del av visar att beslutet fattades efter en rekommendation från statsministerns kansli, som statsminister Jonas Gahr Støre ställer sig bakom. ” Efter en helhetsbedömning har statsministerns kansli kommit fram till att det är konstitutionellt sett mest korrekt att drottningen avböjer utredningskommissionens begäran om ett samtal ”, skriver Støres kommunikationschef Anne Kristin Hjukse i ett mejl till NRK. Kansliet hänvisar till grundlagen och maktdelningsprincipen, som enligt dess tolkning förhindrar medlemmar av kungafamiljen från att avge en förklaring inför en kommission eller ett utskott som utsetts av regeringen. ” Grundlagen ger kungliga prinsar och prinsessor ett särskilt rättsligt skydd, och det antas att detta även gäller drottningen ”, fortsätter Hjukse.

articles.title: Nya chocksiffran om antalet döda
articles.summary: Över 700 000 ryska soldater har dödats i kriget, enligt nya bedömningar från ryska exilmedierna Meduza och Mediazona.
articles.body_text: De ryska förlusterna i kriget är betydligt högre än man tidigare trott, enligt nya bedömningar från ryska exilmedierna Meduza och Mediazona . Över 700 000 ryska soldater uppges ha dödats. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Tidigare i månaden läckte uppgifter om att 450 000 ryssar hade mist livet i kriget efter att hackare slagit till mot ryska statistikbyrån Rosstat. Men siffran uppges nu vara betydligt högre än så. Med hjälp av två pro-ukrainska hackergrupper har man försetts med fler källor, inklusive data från Rysslands befolkningsregister och ett statligt datorsystem som skickar information till ryska statistikbyrån Rosstat. Då landar uppskattningen på ”mer än 700 000” döda ryssar i kriget, enligt Meduza. Michael Kofman vid tankesmedjan Carnegie Endowment for International Peace uppgav för New York Times att Ryssland är på god väg att rekrytera runt 409 000 soldater till 2026. Samtidigt förlorar Ryssland fler soldater än man rekryterar. articles.title: Ilskan mot V: ”Ni har kört sönder”
articles.summary: S-toppen Annika Strandhäll riktar sig till V-veteranen Ulla Andersson efter C-beslutet att återuppta högersamtalen: ”Ni har fullständigt kört sönder detta.”
articles.body_text: S-toppen Annika Strandhäll riktar sig till V-veteranen Ulla Andersson efter Centerpartiets beslut att återuppta högersamtalen. ”Ni har fullständigt kört sönder detta, Ulla. Det är sanningen”, skriver Strandhäll på X. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Centerpartiet återupptar samtalen med M, KD och L . Det meddelade C-ledaren Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist på måndagskvällen. ” Sverige behöver en regering och därför behöver vi öppna fler dörrar, inte stänga några. Vi återupptar därför samtalen med Moderaterna, Kristdemokraterna och Liberalerna ”, skriver Thand Ringqvist i en kommentar till Expressen. Vänsterpartiets vice partiledare Ida Gabrielsson beklagar beskedet och anser att de rödgröna borde ha ”synat” Centerpartiets röda linjer före valet. Hon anklagar Centern för att ha ”vänt på en femöring”. ” I skarpt läge var inte en humanare migrationspolitik viktigare än skattesänkningar. De hoppades bara i stället att vi rödgröna skulle överge våra vallöften under press ”, skriver hon. Centerpartiet återupptar samtalen med M, KD och L . Det meddelade C-ledaren Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist på måndagen. Bakgrunden är att Vänsterpartiet nobbat det så kallade ”startbudet” från S, C och MP , som innehöll löften om sakpolitik och inflytande i regeringen – men utan ministerposter. V sa nej eftersom budet enligt dem inte innehöll några ministerposter eller tillräckligt stort sakpolitiskt inflytande. På tisdagen hålls en ny talmansrunda med samtliga partiledare.
